title: Day 12 — Validate AI Output
prompt: A teammate had an AI write this merge_intervals function, checked one overlapping case, and opened a PR. Review it like you're the one whose name is on the approval. What do you check?

clarifications.answer: Yes — touching intervals like [1,2] and [2,3] must merge into [1,3]. That's one of the bugs.
A nested interval like [2,3] inside [1,10] must keep the outer end (10), not shrink it.
Good instinct — check whether it mutates the caller's list. It does, and it shouldn't.
Input may be unsorted; output should be sorted by start. The sorting part is actually fine.
Empty input returns []. That case is handled correctly.
Three defects total: touching, nested, and input mutation.

hints: Don't just run it — read it and predict inputs that break it. Look hard at the merge condition and the end-assignment.
The condition uses '<' (strict) so touching intervals don't merge; and it sets last[1] = curr[1] instead of max(last[1], curr[1]).
Third bug: 'last' is a reference to an interval from the input, so mutating last[1] mutates the caller's data. Copy the intervals (or build new pairs).
